lessons.statement: When boosted trees outperform raw tabular neural networks, proposed reuse: Proposed conditional application: Compare rank-Gauss normalized swap-noise DAE features with plain neural inputs, then assess the model's ensemble contribution separately from standalone AUC. Proposed check: Compare fold-fitted DAE+NN/plain NN and incremental blend AUC at equal data splits; measure GPU time/memory. Limitation: Approximate recalled gain; huge overcomplete layers and transductive fitting risks require care.

evidence_occurrences.evidence_text: [caption id="attachment_5560" align="aligncenter" width="781"] By using Giulio's dataset (0.96294 single model private score) train and test features are concatenated (2859630 rows) to train an autoencoder neural net. It is an unsupervised learner, that reconstructs itself. Architecture is 98259-4000-4000-4000-2-4000-4000-4000-98259. Middle and output layer is linear, others are ReLU. 20 epochs minibatch SGD on GPU, which took over a day to run. The scatterplot shows the middle layer activations of the train part with targets overlaid (blue=0, red=1). This means that every patient is a dot in this plot.[/caption]

lessons.statement: When tree models may benefit from a complementary learned feature view, proposed reuse: Proposed conditional application: Train a three-hidden-layer swish denoising autoencoder and feed its denoised data into LightGBM.
